Q: "$s = scalar(@a, @b)" causes "Useless use of private array in void context" A:

Use

my $s = @a + @b;

You seem to think that operators perform the same operation and return the same value(s) regardless of context, and that the result is coerced into a scalar in scalar context. This is incorrect.[1] Context is used by operators to the determine the operation to perform and the value to return.

The list/comma operator in scalar context evaluates each item of the list except the last in void context, then it evaluates the last item in scalar context, and it produces the scalar returned by the last item.

my $s = scalar( @a, @b );

my $s = ( @a, @b );   # Identical

is therefore equivalent to

my $s = scalar( do { @a; scalar( @b ) } );

my $s = do { @a; @b };   # Identical

You get just the count of the number of elements in @b. The warning is due to the lack of effect of @a.

print scalar(@a, @b)

List/comma operator in scalar context. Prints the result of @b in scalar context.

print scalar((@a, @b))

No difference. Parens don't create lists in Perl; they just override precedence.

print f(@a, @b)

List/comma operator in list context. Evaluates @a in list context, placing all its values on the stack. Evaluates @b in list context, placing all its values on the stack. Evaluates @_ in scalar context, producing the number of elements in @_. Prints the total number of elements in @a and @b (inefficiently).

does that mean scalar implicitly converts the array passed into an array reference?

No. It just changes the context of the expression provided to it. The expression's result may vary based on context.

  1. If context was a coercion, the following would have the same result:

    my @a = qw( x y z );
say scalar( @a           );   # 3
say scalar( @a[0 .. $#a] );   # z

Q: BackgroundTask iOS 13 Swift A:

BGTaskScheduler simply wont let the app run in the background continuously.

earliestBeginDate = Date(timeIntervalSinceNow: 40) does't causea a task to “execute in 40 seconds”. It only promises to “not execute it before 40 seconds from now”. iOS decides if and when the task actually runs, depending on system context factors I don't remember.

I'm afraid your code contains a few problems:

  1. BGProcessingTask is intended for deferred background work, not keeping a timer alive.

  2. You call task.setTaskCompleted(success: true) immediately. You should call it only after your asynchronous Firebase operation has completed.

  3. MainTableViewController() creates a new view controller which is not the same instance currently displayed by your application. Background work should be moved out of it and into a service/model object.

  4. DispatchQueue.main.async schedules code on the main thread, in the background .

  5. Calling scheduleImageFetcher() again from the handler doesn’t create a reliable periodic task. iOS still controls when the next request runs.

  6. Cancelling all pending requests whenever the app enters the background is no needed, and may work against your scheduling in certain situations.

  7. The task identifier passed when creating BGProcessingTaskRequest must correspond to the identifier registered with BGTaskScheduler and declared in your in Info.plist, under BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers in Info.plist.

So code like

func tickTimer() {
    Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 40, repeats: true) { _ in
        // retrieve Firebase data
    }
}

cannot be used to fetch Firebase data every 40 seconds while the application is in the background. Once iOS suspends the app, your timer stops.

A better approach would be like:

Firebase/server → APNs/FCM push notification → iOS app

A silent push can give the application background execution time to retrieve updated data. But still, they're not guaranteed to be delivered immediately.

  • In short: there is no supported general-purpose API on iOS 13 that lets an application execute tickTimer() every N seconds indefinitely while in the background.

Q: Make sure a Javascript script is first to run? A:

As long as no scripts are dynamically loaded or marked as async or defer, scripts are run or evaluated in the order encountered in the page. So, the first scripts encountered run first.

An externally referenced script file that must be loaded will cause all further javascript execution to wait until that externally referenced file is loaded and parsed and runs.

So, the evaluation order of normal (non-async, non-defer) javascript is 100% determinate as the order it is encountered in the page.

Q: How to know if the address is 64 bit aligned? A:

In order to check alignment of an address, follow this simple rule; Since, byte is the smallest unit to work with memory access A 64 bit address has 8 bytes. (considering, 1 byte = 8bit)

Therefore, Log2(n) = Log2(8) = 3 (to know the power) Where, n is number of bytes.

It means the lower three bits to be zero, in order to follow the alignment rule. E.g. If i have an address, say, 0xC000_0004 Next aligned address would be : 0xC000_0008. You can verify that following address do not have the lower three bits as zero, those are 0xC000_0005 0xC000_0006 0xC000_0007 So, after C000_0004 the next 64 bit aligned address is C000_0008.

Q: How do I resolve the error "ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package"? A:

If you write from . import module, opposite to what you think, module will not be imported from current directory, but from the top level of your package! If you run .py file as a script, it simply doesn't know where the top level is and thus refuses to work.

If you start it like this py -m package.module from the directory above package, then Python knows where the top level is. That's very similar to Java: java -cp bin_directory package.class

Q: Google sign in not working after publishing in play store A:

  • Download Certificates: Navigate to Google Play Console > your app > Release > Setup > App integrity > Download certificates. This downloads a certificates.zip file containing deployment_cert.der, hybrid_classical_cert.der, and hybrid_pqc_cert.der.

  • Extract SHA-1 Fingerprint: Extract the deployment certificate's SHA-1 by running the following command in your terminal: openssl x509 -inform DER -in deployment_cert.der -noout -fingerprint -sha1

  • Register in Google Cloud: Go to the Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials.

  • Add Android OAuth Client: Register the new SHA-1 fingerprint along with your package name as an Android OAuth client. Note that this should be in addition to (not replacing) the classical certificate you already registered.

Q: Mercado Libre API: POST /flex/sites/{site}/items/{item}/v2 returns persistent 409 "can't activate item" for a Full-enrolled item A:

Diagnosis: Non-persistence of "Flex Shipping"

Reproduced and confirmed 3 times, in both directions (activate and deactivate): the checkbox changes, the modal "Check that the stock..." is confirmed, the green box "Done! We saved the changes successfully" appears, but upon refreshing the page, the checkbox (Flex Shipping) reverts to its previous state (unchecked). The console shows no related errors, and all HTTP responses return 200 — hence the error is completely silent for the UI.

Root cause (network evidence, captured by intercepting fetch/XHR on the page): the MELI "omni" form does not perform a direct PUT/PATCH to the item. Everything passes through a single mediating endpoint:

PUT https://vendedores.mercadolibre.cl/publicaciones/app/modificar/omni/api/event-request

Checking/unchecking the checkbox triggers an event with the correct payload:

  • path: .../shipping-dirty
  • body.output.value.marketplace.flex.option = "selected" | "unselected"

This is only a "dirty" state event (it triggers the warning modal and recalculates the UI), not the actual save event.

Clicking the "Confirm" button in the section (the actual "Save") triggers the commit event:

  • path: .../unified-selling-conditions-default
  • body.output = {} ← EMPTY, in all 3 repetitions, both on activation and deactivation

The backend responds with a 200 status code, a rendered brick that locally reflects "selected": true (which is why the UI and the green box show success), but since the actual commit didn't carry any output value, there's nothing to persist against the permanent record of the item. Upon page reload, the actual (never written) state is read, and the checkbox returns to false.

In short: it's a bug in MercadoLibre's frontend within the unified_selling_conditions brick of their "omni" editor — the "Confirm" button handler isn't serializing the accumulated state of shipping-dirty (or other dirty fields) to the final commit event output. The success toast is hardcoded to the 200 response of the event-request, not to a verification that the output actually contained data.
